unit: One workload per experiment, judged on every metric. An experiment is one complete client experiment at N=67108864 (real full-database preprocessing, 1000 measured online queries with retrieval and hint refresh, then the conductor's additional queries: a depth probe, the primary-hint audit, then random distinct queries until the issued queries reach the planned query budget floor(sqrt(N)*ln(N)); the paired reference run is not asked this volume part, which it always serves), run once with the candidate package and once with the reference on identical fresh private database, coin, query and probe seeds. The additional queries are a validity condition, are clocked like measured queries and are read for client storage. Development evaluation has one experiment; the graded evaluation has two independent experiments. All entries are 16 bytes. Seeds are drawn inside each evaluation and are never public, fixed or stored in a dataset.

metrics.name: online_communication_bytes
metrics.means: Per measured query of the experiment, the bytes the trusted transport actually carries: len(request blob) + len(response blob), where the request blob is ReduceRequest(reference request) as sent by the conductor and the response blob is the server handler's return value. The reference is counted at the information-tight encoding of its own messages (16-byte keys, offsets bit-packed at log2(ChunkSize) bits, 16-byte parities): 736+1024=1760 bytes at N=67108864. Messages of the additional queries may not be longer than the longest measured message in their direction (validity), so the measured queries bound them.
metrics.source: judge/harbor/app/quarter_pir/code/conductor/conductor.go (UploadBytes/DownloadBytes appended per query from the blobs passed to and returned by rawrpc.Call); cross-checked against judge/harbor/app/quarter_pir/code/server/replay.go upload/download in judge/evaluator.py; reference sizes from judge/harbor/app/quarter_pir/code/refwire/refwire.go RequestBytes/ResponseBytes and judge/table2_metrics.py reference_message_bytes. Paper: IACR ePrint 2023/1574 Section 6.1 Table 2, Online Communication.
metrics.clears_when: For experiment e: exact positive integer byte counts and candidate_bytes[q] < reference_bytes[q] for every measured query q of e. Equality fails.
metrics.tolerance: none: exact integer accounting of transported bytes.

metrics.name: server_compute_time_ns
metrics.means: Per measured query of the experiment, the elapsed server time in nanoseconds, from the trusted clock in the server entrypoint that starts before pir.HandleQuery receives the request bytes and stops after the complete response bytes exist (request decoding and response encoding are inside). For implementation X, T_X(w) is the median of exactly five measured in-process executions of X's own recorded request q, after one unmeasured full-transcript warm-up pass, in original order, against the same resident database. The handler keeps no state between calls (no package variables; the replay must return exactly the verified responses), so the measured requests represent the additional queries too.
metrics.source: judge/harbor/app/quarter_pir/code/server/server.go TimedQuery; judge/harbor/app/quarter_pir/code/server/replay.go measured passes; judge/evaluator.py replay() median and compare_experiment in judge/table2_metrics.py. Paper Section 6.1 Table 2, server component of online time.
metrics.clears_when: For experiment e: both medians finite and positive and T_candidate(q) < T_reference(q) for every measured query q of e. Equality fails. Reference means the pinned upstream handler behind the new interface, not the expanded-candidate baseline.
metrics.tolerance: none: zero additive and zero relative allowance. Five-run medians are a measurement procedure, not a tolerance.

metrics.name: preprocessing_client_time_minutes
metrics.means: Preprocessing client duration of one experiment, measured by the trusted conductor from sending the coin seed to the client process until the client driver signals that NewClient, Preprocess (including receiving the database stream) and the in-clock ExportHints copy are complete. Reported in minutes; compared as exact integer nanoseconds.
metrics.source: judge/harbor/app/quarter_pir/code/conductor/conductor.go offlineStart..OfflineNs; judge/harbor/app/quarter_pir/code/ec24/ec24_client.go (driver, marker 'p'); judge/table2_metrics.py compare_experiment. Paper Section 6.1 Table 2, Preprocessing Client Time.
metrics.clears_when: For experiment e: candidate offline_elapsed_ns < paired reference offline_elapsed_ns. Equality fails.
metrics.tolerance: none: zero additive and zero relative allowance.

metrics.name: end_to_end_online_time_ms
metrics.means: End-to-end online time of one experiment: the sum of three conductor-clocked intervals (client Query, server round trip of the request, client Reconstruct including hint refresh) over the 1000 measured queries and the depth part of the additional queries, which both paired runs answer identically (the depth part only when both runs completed it); reported in milliseconds per measured query; compared as exact integer nanoseconds. The volume part is clocked the same way (probe_volume_online_ns) and enters the continuous score with the measured queries; the paired reference run skips it. The conductor's own reference-request generation, reduction check and value check lie outside the intervals.
metrics.source: judge/harbor/app/quarter_pir/code/conductor/conductor.go OnlineQueryNs + OnlineTransportNs + OnlineReconstructNs, ProbeOnlineNs, ProbeVolumeOnlineNs; judge/table2_metrics.py paired_online_ns, score_online and compare_experiment. Paper Section 6.1 Table 2, Online Time.
metrics.clears_when: For experiment e: candidate online_elapsed_ns + probe_online_ns < paired reference online_elapsed_ns + probe_online_ns (probe_online_ns of both runs left out when either did not complete the depth part). Equality fails.
metrics.tolerance: none: zero additive and zero relative allowance.

metrics.name: client_storage_bytes
metrics.means: Client storage of one experiment: the peak live state of the client over the online phase, i.e. the largest of the readings taken directly after preprocessing and hint export and, between queries, after the first, one randomly drawn and the last of the measured queries and after every additional query of the depth probe, and in the volume phase after one query drawn at random and after the second-to-last query (few readings among the measured queries because a reading's forced collections slow the queries that follow it). client_storage_volume_bytes is the larger volume-phase reading; the reported client storage is the larger of the two values. A reading is the live Go heap of the client process after two forced garbage collections, minus the same measure taken before NewClient; state released before a reading and rebuilt afterwards counts. The state measured must serve the planned query budget: the additional queries after the measured ones are answered from it. Each reading is taken outside every clock, when no submission goroutine exists; without package variables, cgo or unsafe the heap is the only place client state can live. Measured by the trusted client driver and reported over the harness channel.
metrics.source: judge/harbor/app/quarter_pir/code/ec24/ec24_client.go liveBytes and settle; judge/harbor/app/quarter_pir/code/conductor/conductor.go StorageBytes and StorageVolumeBytes; judge/table2_metrics.py compare_experiment, reference_volume_storage, STORAGE_JITTER_BYTES and REFERENCE_VOLUME_GROWTH_BYTES. Paper: IACR ePrint 2023/1574 Section 6.1 Table 2, client storage.
metrics.clears_when: For experiment e: candidate client_storage_bytes <= paired reference client_storage_bytes + STORAGE_JITTER_BYTES and candidate client_storage_volume_bytes <= reference volume storage + STORAGE_JITTER_BYTES, where the reference volume storage is the paired reference run's client_storage_volume_bytes, or, when that run skipped the volume phase, its client_storage_bytes + REFERENCE_VOLUME_GROWTH_BYTES[db_size] (the reference client's measured growth over the volume phase). Non-inferiority: equality passes.
metrics.tolerance: Measurement jitter only: STORAGE_JITTER_BYTES = 32768, the next power of two above the largest spread of the reference's own measure over repeated runs (19,344 bytes over 14 runs at N=65536; 10,232 bytes over 6 runs at N=67108864). It is not an allowance for additional retained state: one dropped superblock key costs 17,825,792 bytes of hint parities at N=67108864.

beats_reference: Let E contain every experiment of the evaluation. beats_reference = 1 iff the submission passes the patch boundary (only quarter_pir/code/pir/), the source policy, the build, and every validity check of every experiment (each request the client returns equals ReduceRequest of the trusted reference request; every one of the 1000 retrieved values is correct; every additional query (up to the planned query budget in total) that the paired reference run answers is answered by the candidate under the same checks, with no message longer than its longest measured message in that direction; after the depth part of the probe the client returns the canonical record (tag, set parity) of every audited unconsumed primary hint for which the reference client does; the in-clock hint export hash equals the paired reference's; the client process stays under the incidental 4 GiB resident-memory limit; the server replay returns the client-verified responses, follows the resident database and leaves it unchanged), AND every e in E has, on every measured query q of e, candidate_online_communication_bytes[q] < reference_online_communication_bytes[q] and 0 < candidate_server_compute_time_ns[q] < reference_server_compute_time_ns[q], and candidate offline_elapsed_ns < reference offline_elapsed_ns, candidate online time < reference online time over the measured queries and the depth part (end_to_end_online_time_ms), and the candidate's client storage is not above the reference's before and in the volume phase, each up to STORAGE_JITTER_BYTES (client_storage_bytes metric). Equality fails for the four strict metrics and passes for client storage. Missing, invalid, timed-out or incomplete measurements fail. No averaging across workloads, compensation between metrics, tolerance or easier-baseline substitution. The continuous 0-100 score is computed from the candidate's own measurements and is independent of this gate.

solver_feedback.name: candidate_public_server_compute_time_ns_median
solver_feedback.means: On a valid development submission, the median of T_candidate(w) over the 1000 measured queries of the development experiment, in nanoseconds. -1 when no complete valid measurement exists.

solver_feedback.name: candidate_public_online_time_ms_median
solver_feedback.means: The candidate's end-to-end online time of the development experiment in milliseconds per query (the median of a single value). -1 when unavailable.

solver_feedback.name: candidate_public_preprocessing_seconds_large
solver_feedback.means: Candidate preprocessing client time in seconds in the development experiment. -1 when unavailable.

solver_feedback.name: candidate_public_online_communication_bytes_large
solver_feedback.means: Mean request-plus-response bytes per query of the candidate in the development experiment. -1 when unavailable.
solver_feedback.reveals_reference: no - candidate byte counts only; the reference's counts are public constants in the statement.

solver_feedback.name: candidate_public_client_storage_bytes_large
solver_feedback.means: Candidate client storage (the larger of client_storage_bytes and client_storage_volume_bytes) in the development experiment. -1 when unavailable.

solver_feedback.name: candidate_public_validity_code
solver_feedback.means: 0 valid; 1 patch or scope; 2 source policy; 3 build; 4 client crashed, broke the harness protocol or timed out; 5 hint export differs; 6 request is not the reduction of the reference request; 7 wrong retrieved value or failed server call; 8 client process memory limit; 9 server replay check; 10 evaluation time limit; 11 failed an additional query; 12 primary-hint audit failed. -1 when the evaluation did not reach a verdict.
solver_feedback.reveals_reference: no - a coarse category of the candidate's own first failed check; no seed, workload identity or reference measurement.

statement_sentences: The beats_reference gate is the conjunction of five comparisons against the paired reference run: strictly fewer online communication bytes on every query, strictly lower server compute time on every query, strictly lower preprocessing client time in every experiment, strictly lower end-to-end online time in every experiment, and client storage at no point above the reference's in every experiment (up to a fixed measurement-jitter bound); each experiment is one workload judged on all five. Equality fails for the four strict comparisons. Request reduction, correct retrieval of all values, the complete in-clock hint export, the additional queries within the planned query budget, the primary-hint audit after the measured queries, the server replay checks and the source policy are validity conditions. Amortized offline time and preprocessing communication are reported, not compared.
comments: Source provenance: wuwuz/QuarterPIR commit 87b3bb85f5fd388044a6162794f7d6defdf7254b; IACR ePrint 2023/1574, Section 6.1 Table 2. Scope: all computation in package pir (client preprocessing, request generation, reconstruction, hint refresh, server handler, message formats); the trusted harness owns seeds, query issuance, transport, clocks, the value oracle and reporting. Client storage is gated as non-inferiority because online communication can otherwise be bought with client storage; it also enters the continuous score with weight 1/8, so the gate and the score use the same metric set. Amortized offline time is reported but not gated because it has the same numerator and denominator relation as preprocessing client time and would always decide identically. The reference is the unoptimized upstream algorithm behind the new interface (judge/reference.patch). CPU/memory limits and train/final budgets are specified by policy.json.
